title: Security Trust Q&A Handbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working handbook for the security & compliance team and solutions engineers to prepare succinct, evidence-backed responses to customer security questionnaires, RFPs, and Trust Center requests. Focus is on the common sets we see most often: RBAC v2, audit log schema, SIEM export options, and automated evidence packaging.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: solutions engineers, AE security champions, customer security reviewers, and product security SMEs.
- Scope: canned answers, evidence pointers, artifact names, and 'how to assemble' checklists for customer deliveries.
- Not in scope: full legal contract language or finalized SOC reports (link to legal for those).

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Identify question category (authentication, RBAC, logs, SIEM, encryption, data residency).
2) Pick the matching sample answer below.
3) Attach the listed evidence artifacts (S3/Drive paths + audit ids).
4) If evidence is missing, escalate via JIRA-SEC-7123 and copy product-security.

Open items (things we still need to finalize):
- Canonical filenames for exported SIEM bundles (TODO: agreed prefix + timestamp).
- RBAC v2 permission-to-role mapping doc needs a concise diagram (PR#453 needs review).
- Evidence automation runbook for on-demand packaging (owner: Mateo).

Question categories and sample responses (editable templates)

1) Authentication / Identity Management
Q: How do you authenticate API requests?
A: API requests use bearer tokens issued by Redwood's control plane. Tokens are short-lived by default (configurable TTL per customer), and all tokens are bound to a project + role. For private deployments we support customer-managed OIDC providers (see: confluence link for OIDC config).
Evidence: API access logs (audit-index-20260210), token-issuance log snippet (auth-issuance-20260210.json).
Notes: If customer requests proof of rotation policies, attach KMS-key-rotation-schedule.pdf (internal).

2) Authorization / RBAC v2
Q: Can you map roles to least-privilege permissions?
A: Yes. RBAC v2 introduces explicit permission primitives (read:jobs, write:model-config, run:inference) which are composed into roles. We provide two starter role bundles (operator, app-runtime) plus tenant-specific roles. Role bindings are exported as JSON from the control plane and can be audited.
Evidence: rbacexport-<customer>-2026-02-01.json, role-definition-sheet.xlsx
Implementation notes (internal):
- RBAC v2 supports hierarchical resource scoping (org -> project -> model).
- We maintain an internal mapping doc for sensitive perms (see linked PR).
- Outstanding: canonical example for cross-account role delegation (work in progress).

3) Audit log schema and retention
Q: What events are logged and how long are they retained?
A: Our audit schema is event-first with fields: timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, status, ip, region, and optional metadata. System events (infra-level) and user events (API/console) are both captured. Retention depends on plan: hosted default 90 days, dedicated/enterprise configurable up to 7 years (per contract).
Evidence: audit-schema-v3.pdf, sample-audit-file-20260209.json (contains create_model, update_policy, token_revoke events)
Notes: Provide SIEM-consumer mapping doc explaining field mapping for common SIEMs (Splunk, Sumo, Elastic).

4) SIEM export and integration options
Q: How do you integrate audit logs with our SIEM?
A: We support three export modes: push (syslog/HTTP to customer endpoint), pull (S3 bucket with daily manifests), and managed connector (we push to customer Splunk HEC under contract). Exports include compressed NDJSON files that follow the audit schema. Delivery is authenticated (mTLS or presigned S3 URIs) and validated with checksums.
Evidence: siem-export-sample-splunk.ndjson.gz, export-config-screenshot.png
Operational note: For high-frequency customers we recommend push + a periodic S3 archive for replay.

5) Evidence automation (on-demand evidence packs)
Q: Can you produce a zip of artifacts we need for our assessment?
A: Yes. We have a self-serve evidence automation pipeline (WIP) that accepts a request via JIRA with predefined templates (SOC, ISO, custom-questionnaire). The pipeline collects: audit logs for requested window, RBAC exports, config snapshots (KMS settings, network ACLs), and signed checksums. Expected turnaround: 24–72 hours depending on scope.
Evidence: evidence-pack-req-template.md, last-run-report-20260203.json
To assemble: use the automation endpoint (private deploys) or open JIRA with tag 'evidence-automation' for hosted customers.

6) Data flows and residency (short answer)
Q: Where is customer data processed and stored?
A: For hosted customers, inference data is processed in the region selected at onboarding; control plane metadata may be replicated to our primary regions for observability. Dedicated and Private deployments allow fully regional or on-prem processing per contract.
Evidence: data-flow-diagram.pdf, region-config-2026-01.csv

7) Incident response and breach notification
Q: How do you notify customers of security incidents?
A: Incidents are classified per our IR runbook. For impacting incidents affecting customer data or availability, we alert primary contacts within SLA windows defined in the contract (usually 24 hours for medium/high). A post-incident report is produced with forensic artifacts, timeline, and mitigation steps.
Evidence: ir-runbook-v2.pdf, sample-incident-communication-20250115.pdf

Assembly checklists (for canned deliveries)
- Small ask (email Q&A): pick matching sample answer, attach 1–2 evidence artifacts, cc legal if scope hits contracts.
- Medium ask (customer audit questionnaire): use the questionnaire template, map each question to one evidence item, attach RBAC export + 7 days of audit logs + config snapshot.
- Large ask (SOC-like assessment): route to product-security + legal; collect retention policy, system architecture, KMS proofs, SIEM export manifests, and signed evidence pack.

Working templates (placeholders - replace before sending)
- [TEMPLATE] Short answer: "We log X, Y, Z and can provide an export on request."
- [TEMPLATE] Evidence pointer: "See artifact: <artifact-name> (S3:/redwood-evidence/<org>/<id>/)"
- [TEMPLATE] Redaction note: "We will redact PII from event payloads as agreed; sign off required via SLAs."

- Audit schema docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Audit-Schema-v3

- SIEM mappings: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/SIEM-Mappings
- Infra PR that changed export format: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/453

Owners and escalation

- Evidence automation owner: Mateo Ruiz (eng-ops)
- RBAC spec lead: Priya Kapoor (applied-ml)
- SIEM & integrations: Oliver Grant (observability)
- Escalation channel: #sec-evidence (Slack) and JIRA-SEC-7123

Action items (next steps)
- Finalize canonical SIEM bundle filename pattern (owner: Oliver, due 2026-03-20).
- Add example of redaction process for PII in exported logs (owner: Priya, due 2026-03-18).
- Draft a one-page Trust Center blurb summarizing the export capabilities for public consumption (owner: Ava, due 2026-03-25).

Notes to self / informal brainstorming (raw):
- Could we add a small interactive checklist in the Console for 'Request evidence pack'? Low effort, high value.
- Consider a non-prod demo tenant for showing SIEM ingestion to customers during security reviews.
- Think about standardizing retention labels on artifacts so SRE can auto-attach them to tickets.

End of WIP.
Please add edits directly and tag owners for each section you change.
